fix: Add `GestureArena::disposition(&self, key, member) -> GestureDisposition` in crates/incular-gestures/src/arena.rs that scans the stream in place without collecting (same result as `disposition_for(&entries(key), member)`). Replace the per-event Vec with it: drop line 1101 and change line 1108 to `let disposition = self.input.gesture_arena.disposition(key, candidate.member);`. Disjoint field borrows keep the `active_gestures` borrow valid.

Add `GestureArena::has_entries(&self, key) -> bool` in crates/incular-gestures/src/arena.rs applying the same filter as `entries` without building the Vec, then write `let handled = self.input.gesture_arena.has_entries(key);`. This runs on every pointer event that reaches the stream, only to test emptiness.

Keep the four buffers (accepts, rejects, callbacks, scale_updates) as reusable scratch fields on the input state. At the start of this function take each with `std::mem::take`, call `clear()`, and at the end `clear()` and store it back. Taking and restoring keeps capacity across events, so the pushes made on every drag move stop reallocating. Without the restore the capacity is lost, so do not skip it.

Swap with a retained spare buffer instead of taking: keep `fling_spare: Vec<ScrollFlingDriver>` on the input state, then `let mut drivers = std::mem::take(&mut self.input.fling_spare); std::mem::swap(&mut drivers, &mut self.input.scroll_flings);` and iterate `for mut driver in drivers.drain(..)`. At the end, `self.input.fling_spare = drivers;` (empty, capacity kept). Each frame during a fling currently reallocates the driver Vec from zero when the survivors are pushed back.

This runs every frame while any press is active. Reuse a scratch `Vec<GestureArenaKey>` field: take it, `clear()`, `extend(self.input.active_gestures.keys().copied())`, iterate with `for key in keys.iter().copied()` (the loop calls `&mut self` methods, so the buffer must be detached from self while iterating), and store it back at the end.

Remove the matching drivers in place instead of rebuilding the Vec: `for driver in self.input.scroll_flings.extract_if(.., |d| &d.controller == controller) { held_velocity = driver.simulation.dx(driver.elapsed); driver.activity.finish(); }`. `Vec::extract_if` is stable (Rust 1.87+) and the MSRV is 1.99. Order of the surviving drivers is preserved and the call stops allocating.

Filter before cloning so only the survivors are cloned: `.filter(|attachment| attachment.controller().has_pending_ballistic()).map(|attachment| attachment.controller().clone())`. This runs every frame from `pump_scroll_flings` and clones every attached controller (an Rc and a DependencySource clone) before discarding most of them.

Same as the handed-over collect above: filter on `attachment.controller().has_pending_animation() || attachment.controller().has_pending_settle()` first, then `.map(|attachment| attachment.controller().clone())`. Runs every frame from `start_scroll_animations` and clones every attached controller before the predicate.

`callbacks` is a `Box<GestureCallbacks>` (crates/incular-widgets/src/tree/specs.rs:546). Every press clones the whole struct, about 20 `Option<Rc<dyn Fn..>>` fields, per candidate ancestor. Change the spec field to `Rc<GestureCallbacks>` and return `Option<Rc<GestureCallbacks>>` here (`Some(Rc::clone(callbacks))`), so the per-press cost is one refcount increment. Callers at lines 36, 39, 89, 116 and 766 then use the Rc.

This allocates a fresh no-op Rc on every call for each draggable candidate on a press. Create the no-op once when the tree is built (a field such as `noop_drag_update: Rc<dyn Fn(DragUpdateDetails)>`) and `Rc::clone` it here.
